mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5% mean) in periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for two months, as measured by a one-tailed t-test at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in mortgage applications (HOUST) signals weakening household demand and housing market stress, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and drives S&P 500 declines over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1% mean) during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY and HOUST rises month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5% mean) when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month by > 0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1% mean) during four consecutive months of > 0.5% monthly INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS) and a fall in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals a precautionary savings behavior that foreshadows a near-term pullback in consumer spending and weaker corporate revenues, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous month AND GDPC1 < previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5% mean) when RSAFS rises and GDPC1 falls simultaneously in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate of more than 0.75 percentage points signals an aggressive tightening stance, which immediately raises interest rate sensitivity of equities and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1% mean) following a single-month FEDFUNDS increase of more than 0.75 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth above 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that feeds into higher wage pressures and inflation, which in turn raises discount rates and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days under a high-inflation regime.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.5% for 3 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL > 3% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5% mean) when PAYEMS grows faster than 0.5% per month for three months and CPIAUCSL exceeds 3% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above 5% YoY for six consecutive months signals a robust housing recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month AND HOUST YoY > 5% for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1% mean) during six consecutive months of > 5% YoY HOUST growth with month-over-month increases.
